passage: Rain drummed on the roof, so recess was indoors, and the whole class was squeezed between desks. Nazia watched Kavya's group giggle over sticker books in the corner. She wanted to sit with them so badly that her stomach ached. Then Kavya said, "You can sit here if you laugh at Bidisha's accent." Nazia's mouth went dry. Bidisha, her friend, was two rows away, drawing quietly. Nazia said, "No, thanks," and walked back. Bidisha looked up and moved her bag off the seat next to her. "I saved you one," she said. Nazia sat down. The sticker giggles kept going, but she found she could breathe.

qa.a: It was raining, so recess was indoors.

qa.q: What was Nazia feeling as she watched Kavya's group?
qa.a: She envied them and wanted to belong, so much that her stomach ached.

qa.q: What could Nazia do if the popular group asks her again later?
qa.a: She can keep saying no to being unkind, stay with friends who accept her, and tell a teacher if the pressure continues.

qa.q: How might Bidisha have felt when Nazia walked back to her?
qa.a: Bidisha probably felt glad and touched that Nazia chose her, as her saved seat shows.

grounding: A child envies the popular group and is asked to mock a friend; she says no and finds real friendship.

passage:
Monday. Reena watched the popular girls laughing by the water cooler, all with matching butterfly clips. She bought the same clips with her pocket money and practised their giggle in the mirror.
Wednesday. Usha, the leader, finally waved her over. 'You can hang out with us. But first, go tell Ruchi her lunch stinks. Loudly.' Ruchi was sitting alone, eating poha. Reena's stomach twisted. She had wanted this for months.
Thursday. Reena didn't go to the water cooler. She sat down next to Ruchi. 'Your poha smells nice, actually. Is there onion in it?' Ruchi looked up, surprised, and smiled. Reena took the butterfly clips out of her hair and put them in her pencil box. She didn't feel sorry at all.

qa.q: What did the popular girls wear?
Why did Reena's stomach twist on Wednesday?
qa.a: She was torn: she envied the group and wanted in, but being cruel to Ruchi felt wrong.

qa.q: What was the wise choice on Thursday, and why?
qa.a: Sitting with Ruchi instead of joining; belonging that required cruelty cost too much.

qa.q: What might Ruchi have felt when Reena sat down?
qa.a: Surprised and relieved to have someone kind beside her after eating alone.

grounding: Over several days a girl who envies a popular group refuses when they ask her to be cruel, and chooses kindness instead.

passage: 'Ayesha, you've been staring at those girls on the bus for a week. Let your Gurleen Aunty tell you a story. At your age, in Ludhiana, there was a group of girls everyone wanted to be with. They had the best tiffins and the loudest laughs. I wanted in so badly I dreamed about it. One day their leader said I could join, if I stopped wearing my kara and stopped speaking Punjabi at school, because it was "too village". I went home and stood at the mirror, turning the kara on my wrist. It was my grandmother's. The next morning I told them no. I cried in the washroom after. But by winter I had two friends who laughed at my Punjabi jokes, and I still have them now.'

qa.q: What did the leader ask young Gurleen to stop wearing?
What was young Gurleen feeling as she turned the kara at the mirror?
qa.a: Torn and sad; she badly wanted to belong, but the kara was her grandmother's and part of who she was.

qa.q: What choice in the story turned out wise, and why?
qa.a: Saying no to the group; the price was changing herself, and by winter she had friends who liked her as she was.

qa.q: How might the group's leader have seen Gurleen's refusal?
qa.a: Perhaps surprised or offended, since she was used to girls changing themselves to join.

grounding: An aunt recalls envying a popular group and refusing to join when the price was giving up who she was.
